messages:
pete: Heads-up — running into a weird type-resolution mismatch consuming @redwood/inference from an edge project. Generics on the client vanish unless we explicitly import types from a deep path. Anyone seen exports/types path issues?

anya: yup. Often the package's `exports` map points runtime import to `dist/esm/index.js` but `types` points to `dist/index.d.ts` (root). TS resolution can choose a different types file depending on moduleResolution and TS version. Can you paste the package.json exports?

pete: exports for the SDK: `{".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }}`. We bundle with esbuild for Cloudflare and notice `client.request` param types become `any`. Local `tsc --noEmit` is fine.

sam: that mismatch is suspicious. TS tries to pair the import entry with a matching types entry. If `types` doesn't mirror the conditional path (e.g., an ESM-specific d.ts), you can hit fallback semantics. Recommend SDK authors set `exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts" } }` so the ESM import and types path align.

anya: also check `typesVersions` — some packages use it to remap for TS versions which can cause older TS to pick a flattened CJS-style d.ts that uses `export =` and loses generics. What TS version are you on locally vs CI?

pete: dev machines vary (4.9/5.0), CI runs 5.2. Edge bundler pipeline uses esbuild and a legacy ts-node for dev-run (which embeds TS 4.9).

nora: that explains it: older TS + typesVersions fallback -> differing declaration selected. Two mitigation paths: 1) consumer-side: add a small ambient augmentation in your repo to re-declare the client generic methods, 2) infra-side: make esbuild externalize `@redwood/inference` so the bundle doesn't shadow d.ts resolution, 3) SDK-side: publish ESM-aligned types and avoid `export =` in emitted d.ts.

sam: for the augmentation you can create `types/redwood-augment.d.ts` with:```ts
declare module '@redwood/inference' {
  interface RedwoodClient<T = any> {
    request<TIn, TOut = any>(opts: { input: TIn; }): Promise<TOut>;
  }
}
```
That merges and usually fixes inference in both tsc and tsserver. Ugly but effective short-term.

pete: augmentation works but feels fragile. Any CI checks we can add to catch regressions earlier?

anya: add a tiny consumer smoke test in the SDK repo that runs a minimal ESM project consuming the package and executes `tsc --noEmit`. Also add a bundling smoke that runs esbuild on a sample edge worker and ensures compile-time types survive. That would have caught this.

nora: on the bundler side, set `importsNotUsedAsValues: 'preserve'` in tsconfig used by esbuild and enable `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` for modern ESM handling. esbuild sometimes rewrites imports into runtime shims which severs TS contextual typing — preserving type-only imports helps.

sam: there's also a Deno/Cloudflare difference: Deno often expects a pure ESM types file and will fail if package has CJS-leaning dts with `export =`. If you need Deno compatibility, SDK should publish `dist/esm/index.d.ts` with standard `export`/`declare` constructs.

pete: I'll file an infra task to externalize the SDK in our edge bundler for now and open an upstream SDK issue asking for ESM-aligned types + a tiny edge/ts compile CI job. docs-bot: please create the SDK issue with label dx/typing.

docs-bot: Created issue #4771: "types: align exported types with ESM entrypoint; avoid CJS-style emit to preserve generics for edge consumers" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4771 :robot_face:

anya: one more subtle note — if the SDK d.ts re-exports generated types via `export =` or `namespace` merging, TS will often widen generics across module boundaries. Ask SDK to emit explicit generic method declarations (e.g., `request<TIn, TOut>(opts: ...)`) instead of `...any...`. Also add a `types` export for the ESM conditional to avoid fallback.

pete: thanks — going to push the augmentation + externalize in CI while we wait for SDK fix. Will follow up on issue with a tiny repro that demonstrates the typesVersions fallback across TS 4.9 vs 5.x. :thumbsup:
